body:
Use `Jinv` for the inverse of the inertia for consistency with the rest of the code:
```suggestion
  double Jinv = 0.0; ///< 1 / spin inertia about the axle [1/(slug*ft^2)]
```
You should remove `LeverArm` now that you have introduced the moment jacobian, it would simplify the code using it everywhere.
Once having removed `LeverArm`, you will no longer need the lambda function `moment`.

This code should be located in the new method `ConfigureWheelSpinRows`. With the current code, it is far from obvious that when a wheel is accounted for, then the friction coefficient is `staticFFactor * staticFCoeff`. The reason for that is that with the current code in the PR, I was expecting the friction coefficient of `ftRoll` to be updated in `ConfigureWheelSpinRows`.

These variable names are misleading because `roll` is actually the direction of the roll friction force (unit vector) and `axle` is not the axle direction but the axle **position** with respect to the CG. And since the code is historically using *lever arm* to designate this position, then do so here as well.

Do not export the so-called *absolute spin rate*. Instead export the wheel spin rate measured with respect to the body frame. The latter is the spin rate that the Flight Control System and the Anti Blocking System will have access to (using a phonic wheel) in the real world.

Also it is the spin rate relative to the aircraft that 3D modelers need to display the wheels since models are generally organized through a hierarchy of bodies, each one being positioned relative to its parent in the hierarchy.

body:
There is no "absolute" in JSBSim. Instead tell that it is the spin rate measured with respect to the NED frame.
```suggestion
  double Rate = 0.0;       ///< spin rate about the axle measured in the NED frame [rad/s]
```
And the `continue` keyword to avoid an `else` is debatable...
